THREE THINGS A READER SHOULD KNOW. (1) The test was administered in two gender-matched forms and the item code does not record which form a child saw (108 girls, 96 boys), so item_text and option_text carry BOTH forms in one field, marked '[girls' form] ... [boys' form] ...'; neither form is invented, both are verbatim. The girls' form is internally inconsistent about 'friends' - items ONE15szPREZ_KOL and ONE20szKOL_UBR read 'kolegow' (masculine) where the other six KOL items read 'kolezanek'; transcribed as printed. (2) The 32 TWO* item codes are not new questions: they are the SAME 32 items re-administered two weeks later to the test-retest subsample (n=27 vs n=204 for the ONE* codes), which the IRW table encodes as extra items rather than as a wave. TWO<n><block> therefore ships the same wording as ONE<n><block><pair>. (3) resp 1 = the picture named FIRST in the item sentence (picture A on the printed page), resp 2 = the picture named second (B); this is established from the deposit's own recoded columns, not assumed - see verify_PMT_Trzcinska_2023_PMT.R. The English in the _translated columns was assembled by IRW: every phrase is the paper's own English (its list of the eight pictures, its two question stems and its two printed example sentences, PLOS ONE 18(8):e0290512), but 30 of the 32 sentences are not printed anywhere as sentences, so translation_source is recorded as machine_translation rather than study_supplied. Rights: the PMT is the authors' own new instrument, published CC BY 4.0 and deposited in full on OSF under CC BY 4.0; no fee, no non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is stated by the rights holder, so nothing blocks. WORDING IS AVAILABLE; THE CODE->WORDING MAPPING IS NOT. The instrument is the Teachers' Remote Work Context Assessment Scale (TRWCAS / EACTDR). Its construction paper, Cunha et al., Psico-USF 29:e272895, doi:10.1590/1413-8271202429e272895 (CC BY 4.0), prints English wording for 31 pool items in Table 2 and quotes 7 more in the Discussion; a sibling technical report from the same group (Rodrigues, UVA, ww2.uva.ce.gov.br/apps/view/book_html/ebook_ptp_0125/rodrigues_relatorio_tecnico.html) prints the administered Portuguese for all 33 retained items and, in its visible R code, the code->factor assignment using exactly the ct1..ct40 naming this deposit uses (organizacao: ct1,ct4,ct7,ct8,ct12,ct13,ct14,ct17,ct19,ct21,ct22,ct23,ct24,ct30,ct37; condicoes: ct9,ct16,ct18,ct20,ct26,ct33,ct36,ct38; relacoes: ct5,ct6,ct10,ct11,ct15,ct27,ct29,ct32,ct35,ct39). Cross-reading those two sources recovers Portuguese+English for 19 of this table's 23 items and English for the other 4 (the pool items the construction paper rejected: 2, 3, 25, 31). BUT the live data contradicts the hypothesis that this deposit's ct_N is that same pool item N. Under it, mean within-factor r = 0.211 vs mean between-factor r = 0.216 (n=235, 19 assignable items) -- no block structure at all; only 5 of 17 items load strongest on their hypothesised subscale. Near-synonymous pairs are near zero (ct_6 'no autonomy over class CONTENT' x ct_32 'no autonomy over teaching METHODS' r=0.066; ct_33 'noisy workspace' x ct_36 'uncomfortable workspace' r=0.183) while semantically unrelated pairs top the whole matrix (ct_31 'borrowed computer' x ct_32 'no autonomy over methods' r=0.782; ct_27 'no manager support' x ct_31 r=0.751; ct_1 'no rest breaks' x ct_2 'no integration with other teachers' r=0.684). Item means rank-correlate only rho=0.204 with the developers' own basic-education sample over the 19 shared items, and every hypothesised socio-professional item sits +1.1 to +2.2 above it (ct_29 3.86 vs 1.66; ct_15 4.03 vs 2.04) -- implausible content-wise for university faculty. Conclusion: this deposit's ct_N numbering is most likely the university ADAPTATION's own numbering (the deposit's own column order is not even monotone: ...ct_25, ct_23, ct_29, ct_27...), not the original pool's, and shipping the pool wording against these codes would ship a confidently-wrong mapping.
